newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair COO targets sustained profits.
newsitem.headline: Swissair COO targets sustained profits.

text.p: Jeffrey Katz, newly-appointed chief operating officer (COO) of the Swissair airline, said his mission was sustained profitability for the carrier and he would not have left American Airlines if he did not believe he would be successful.

Katz, also chief executive designate at Swissair, the core airline of the SAirGroup, also told the Swiss-American Chamber of Commerce he believed the European airline sector would be facing a turbulent period, but this represented an opportunity for Swissair and a personal challenge.

He doubted the industry in Europe would follow the same pattern the United States because Europeans have learned from the U.S. experience and there were many more restrictions in Europe, including geographical.
"But we'll see prices sinking, irrational competition and see people giving money to people that don't know what they are doing...the opposite to risk adverse," he said.

Katz took up his position at Swissair on April 1, leaving American Airlines where he was managing director of passenger sales for the Western U.S. and president of the Sabre Travel Information Network.

The goal of SAirGroup's chief executive Philippe Bruggisser is to make Swissair's flight operations profitable by 1998. Bruggisser recently said Swissair's loss in flight operations -- a result that is not published -- was some 120 million Swiss francs in 1996.

Katz, whose appointment at the national flag carrier raised eyebrows in Switzerland, said he had often been asked if he was a better manager than a Swiss would be. His answer was: "I am not better, just different. I have been brought here as a leader and will create a team of individuals and our mission is sustained profitability."

Asked if he was convinced Swissair could be profitable, Katz said and profitability and success were the same in the way his performance was measured and he would not have made the move from American Airlines if, "I didn't believe this would be successful."
He would seek to infuse Swissair with what he described as the American trait of looking at everything in a "terribly positive" manner.
But he noted that such positive thinking was not so much an American "thing, but an attitude" and one of its favourite sayings was "motivation is performance."
"The Swissair product is good, the people are good and the market potential is good and Swissair people will make the company successful," Katz said.

Commenting on a question about a deterioration in Swissair's service at the Zurich airport, Katz said the introduction of a fourth wave of traffic at the airport was part of making Zurich into a larger hub and there were still things to be learned.
"Reliability is part of our image and that is part of the standards that we will fulfill. But we have a few things to learn about operating a hub," Katz said.
"Right now Zurich is on its way to becoming a bigger hub in the European market place."
